sections.what_happened: After Ukraine reported its Air Alert app compromised (false radiation-threat alerts sent nationwide; air force: 'There is no radiation threat', spokesman Yuriy Ignat confirmed hack to AFP — already recorded in the 0500 scan as a missed catch-up), Russia's emergencies ministry said its emergency warnings app came under a 'massive cyberattack' enabling attackers to send 'false information' to the public. The exchange came as the six-day Oleshky-area truce (Oct 27-Nov 1, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump) ended Sunday after Russia refused an extension (Ukraine human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets). Zelensky's linked bargain also stands: Kyiv would stop hitting Russian refineries if Washington supplied Patriot interceptors.
sections.what_verified: The Hindu reporting; Ukraine air force statement via AFP; Russia emergencies ministry statement; Lubinets truce-end statement.
sections.what_disputed: Attribution for either hack is unproven in-window: neither side names the attacker, and false-alert content differs (radiation threat in Ukraine; unspecified false information in Russia). Do not present as confirmed mutual cyber warfare by a named actor. The Oleshky truce itself is under an owner-review hold in TOTW production (per standing locks) — this item reports the truce's end, it does not reopen the Oleshky video.
sections.why_matters: Both alert apps hacked on the night the truce died — the new front is the warning system itself. Monitor-only: no named attacker, no casualty claim to hang a Short on.
